t: You're looking at the ruins of St Dunstan-in-the-East, a parish church on St Dunstan's Hill, about halfway between London Bridge and the Tower of London. The church was largely destroyed in the Second World War, and the ruins are now a public garden, looked after by the City of London Corporation. Christopher Wren is named as its designer, and he was the man given the job of rebuilding 52 City churches after the Great Fire. The name comes from Dunstan, the Anglo-Saxon monk who became Bishop of London and later Archbishop of Canterbury, and was made a saint.
